'Spam@x.com' bypasses a BLACKLISTED_GUEST_EMAILS entry 'spam@x.com' and is created as an attendee, and a case-variant of an existing attendee's email passes the filter so createMany inserts a duplicate attendee row that then receives duplicate emails and ICS entries.

adjudication.rationale: In `addGuests.handler.ts`, `blacklistedGuestEmails` are normalized via `.toLowerCase()`, but the filter compares them with `!blacklistedGuestEmails.includes(guest)` where `guest` is not lowercased. The existing-attendee dedupe is also case-sensitive: `guest === attendee.email`. Since the input schema (`z.string().email()`) does not enforce lowercase, a case-variant like `Spam@x.com` can bypass both the blacklist and the “already an attendee” check, leading to unintended attendee creation (and downstream case-sensitive checks like `newGuests.includes(attendee.email)` in `sendAddGuestsEmails` will also behave inconsistently).
